rule: Slot rule unchanged: PASS 1 exact title after normalisation, PASS 2 ordinal slot (unclaimed after PASS 1, unique both ways), PASS 3 recorded absence under its mechanism. What changed is the NORMALISATION and one operator adjudication.

decisions_applied.1_box_drawing_dash: Every non-ASCII character folded to a space. MEGA filenames mix a real box-drawing dash (U+2500) with the same bytes mis-decoded into Latin letters. Guessing which mangling occurred is unreliable, so the whole class is folded. Safe because non-ASCII in this corpus is decorative separators only, never identifying content.
decisions_applied.2_call_type_prefix: Explicit alias table: branded and bare call-type words (guest/coaching/theory call, call, calls) collapse to one canonical ' call ', and the brand mark is written 'NHB+' by one file family and 'NHB' by the other, so it is normalised too. Not a heuristic - an enumerated table.
decisions_applied.adjudication: 2025/02 'Offer Fundamentals' == 'How To Make Offers That Are Built For Scale'. Operator ruling, recorded as ONE pair with its reason and deliberately NOT generalised into a rule.

CORRECTION_TO_THE_PREVIOUS_ARTIFACT.call_count: 198, NOT the 210 previously reported. The earlier count treated an mp3 and its mp4 as two calls. They are two encodings of one recording.
CORRECTION_TO_THE_PREVIOUS_ARTIFACT.verification: 268 media files, 70 titles carrying both an mp3 and an mp4, 198 distinct calls. 268 - 70 = 198 closes exactly. Of those 70 pairs, 12 showed durations differing by exactly ONE SECOND (e.g. 3:31:21 vs 3:31:22) - the normal rounding difference between two encodings of the same recording, not evidence of two different calls.

deliberately_not_normalised: '#3' vs '3' - content-bearing, folding it risks merging genuinely distinct parts.

The leading ' - ' after a date on 2025/02 media files - this is the LAST systematic divergence found, and folding a stray leading separator is low-risk, but it is left visible rather than silently absorbed. RECOMMENDED as a future decision, not applied here.

Truncated surnames ('Kirklan' vs 'Kirkland') and year mismatches (2024 vs 2025) - these are typos in the source, not a naming convention. Absorbing them would be inventing a rule the corpus does not support.
bugs_found_while_building_v2: LEAD_NUM matched a hyphen as well as a dot, so '01-20-2025' lost its month and every title in the corpus was truncated to '20-2025'. This silently destroyed the date component of every join key.
The brand mark 'NHB+' was never normalised, so 'nhb+ call' could never equal 'nhb call' and the 11 prefix orphans persisted after the alias table was added.
The adjudication tested `summary_title in calls`, but `calls` holds MEDIA titles only, so the operator ruling could never fire.
The adjudication record stored a reconstructed filename missing the ' AI Summary' suffix, naming a file that does not exist.
